title: Lemongrass Coconut Chicken with Basil
description: Bruised lemongrass infuses a silky coconut braising sauce that clings to short pieces of chicken thigh.

ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken thighs
ingredients.note: Use plain, unenhanced poultry. Remove visible fat before weighing.

ingredients.name: fresh lemongrass stalks
ingredients.note: Trim tops and dry outer layers; use the pale lower sections. Remove before serving.

ingredients.name: plain light coconut milk
ingredients.note: Unsweetened and unseasoned; stir until smooth.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Use plain chicken-and-water broth without a vegetable blend or added seasoning.

ingredients.name: fresh ginger
ingredients.note: Thin slices, left large enough to remove. Remove before serving.

ingredients.name: fresh basil
ingredients.note: Large leafy sprig, left whole. Remove before serving.

steps.title: Release the lemongrass aroma
steps.text: Bruise {lemongrass} with the flat of a knife on a cutting board. Cut each stalk into large pieces that can be lifted out.

steps.title: Infuse the coconut broth
steps.text: Combine the bruised stalks, {ginger}, {broth} and {coconut} in the PossibleCooker. Set Sear/Sauté HIGH with the lid off until just simmering, then LOW for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Poach the chicken
steps.text: Cut {chicken} across the grain into 3/4-inch pieces. Add to the broth and restore the simmer, using HIGH briefly if needed. Cook uncovered on LOW for 10–16 minutes. Pull each piece when its center reaches 175°F and hold covered in a little coconut broth.

steps.title: Steep the basil
steps.text: Turn off the heat, immerse {basil} in the hot broth and steep for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Strain the sauce
steps.text: Pour the broth through a fine sieve into a heatproof jug. Remove the fibers, ginger and basil, then return all the infused liquid to the pot.

steps.title: Season the broth
steps.text: Stir in {aminos} and restore a gentle simmer on Sear/Sauté with the lid off.

steps.title: Bind the coconut sauce
steps.text: Stir in the slurry and maintain a gentle bubble for 1 minute, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon. Thin with a splash of hot water if needed to keep it pourable.

steps.title: Serve generously
steps.text: Return the chicken and its juices to the coconut sauce off heat. Divide the pieces and all of the sauce among four bowls.

notes: Sauce yield: About 2 to 2 1/2 cups for four, or 1/2 cup per serving. Make ahead: Bruise the stalks and slice the ginger a day ahead and refrigerate them. Strain the infused liquid thoroughly before serving. Option A includes ginger. For gentler Option B, leave it out and use just one bruised lemongrass stalk for four servings. Chill leftovers promptly in shallow portions and refrigerate for up to 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze the chicken in sauce for up to 2 months. Stir thoroughly when reheating to reunite the coconut fat and liquid. Fridge reheat: Warm one portion covered in its sauce in a HexClad skillet over medium-low, loosening with a splash of water if needed. Stir or turn the chicken gently, checking from 6 minutes, until it reaches 165°F throughout. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then follow the fridge reheating directions and stir the sauce smooth. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 237 kcal, 28.6 g protein, 4.8 g total carbohydrate, 10.5 g fat, 0.0 g fiber, 210 mg sodium. Includes the measured broth and sauce. Sodium varies with your broth.
